name: stacktree
description: Publish the pages you build to a private link that opens in any browser, with no account for the viewer. Links are unguessable by default, can carry a passcode or be limited to a company email domain, expire on a schedule, and update in place so a link you have already sent never goes stale.

interface.shortDescription: Publish HTML to a private link
interface.longDescription:
Stacktree turns the pages ChatGPT and Codex build for you into a private link anyone can open in a browser.

Ask for a report, a proposal, a dashboard or a one-page site, then publish it in the same conversation. The page opens with no account and no sign-in, on a link that is private and unguessable by default. Revising the page replaces it in place, so a link you have already sent shows the latest version.

Stacktree is built for work that leaves the conversation: client deliverables, stakeholder updates, and anything someone outside your chat needs to see.
- Add a passcode, or limit a page to people with an email address at one company.
- Mint a named link for each recipient and see who opened it.
- File pages under a client space, so everything for one customer lives at one address.
- Let clients comment on the page itself, with no account. ChatGPT can read their comments, fix the page and mark each one resolved.
- Set a page to expire, take it down, or put an earlier version back.

Pages are private by default. Links are unguessable, pages ask search engines not to index them, and a check before publishing looks for personal data and secrets in the page.

Stacktree needs a Stacktree account. You connect it the first time you publish.
capabilities: Publish HTML pages to private links
Update a page in place at the same link
Named share links that show who opened them
defaultPrompt: Turn this into a web page and give me a private link to send.
Put a passcode on my latest Stacktree page.
Show me the comments clients left on my pages.

positive.prompt: Use Stacktree to publish a one-page HTML site for a fictional coffee shop called Ember and give me the link.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the page's id and a private stacktr.ee link. The link opens in any browser without signing in, and the reply says when it expires or that it does not.

positive.description: Add a passcode to an existing page
positive.prompt: Password-protect my latest Stacktree page with the passcode sesame.
positive.expected_behavior: set_password returns ok. Opening the link now shows a passcode prompt, and sesame unlocks the page.

positive.prompt: List my Stacktree pages and tell me how many there are.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the demo account's pages with titles and links, including the seeded Crumb bakery page and the Q3 report. Read-only, so no confirmation is asked for.

positive.prompt: Change the headline on my Crumb page to 'Fresh daily'.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks to confirm, because the update replaces the page. update_site then returns the same id and link, and the link shows the new headline. No new link is created.

positive.description: Read client comments and resolve one
positive.prompt: Check the comments on my Crumb page and mark the first one resolved.
positive.expected_behavior: list_feedback returns the page's two seeded comments, unresolved first. resolve_feedback marks one resolved with a short note and returns ok.

negative.description: Publishing a code package, not a web page
negative.prompt: Publish my npm package to the registry.
Post this update to my LinkedIn and X accounts.

negative.description: Deploying a full-stack app with a database
negative.prompt: Deploy my Next.js app with a Postgres database to production.

review.commerce_description: Stacktree does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release. Publish the pages ChatGPT and Codex build to a private link, with five skills for client deliverables, run reports, daily briefs and status pages that pick the right gate, expiry and link.
